task_snapshot.title: Implement greedy word wrapping in wrap_text
task_snapshot.description: wrap_text is declared with a documented contract but raises NotImplementedError.
task_snapshot.problem_statement:
`textkit.wrap_text(text, width)` is declared in `src/textkit/wrap.py` but raises NotImplementedError. Implement it according to its docstring.

Required behaviour:

- Return a list of lines, each at most `width` characters long.
- Split the input on runs of whitespace; a run of whitespace is a single word separator, so `wrap_text("a   b", 10) == ["a b"]`.
- Pack words greedily: fill the current line while the next word still fits, then start a new line.
- A word longer than `width` cannot fit on any line, so hard-split it across consecutive lines.
- Input that contains no words returns an empty list.
- Raise ValueError when `width` is less than 1.
- Lines must carry no leading or trailing whitespace, and word order must be preserved.

Example: `wrap_text("the quick brown fox", 10)` returns `["the quick", "brown fox"]`.
acceptance_criteria: Words are packed greedily and kept in order
Words longer than width are hard-split
Whitespace runs collapse to a single separator
Empty or whitespace-only input returns an empty list
hints: str.split() with no argument already collapses whitespace runs.

"""URL slug generation."""

from __future__ import annotations


def slugify(text: str, sep: str = "-") -> str:
    """Convert ``text`` into a lowercase URL slug.

    Runs of non-alphanumeric characters collapse into a single separator, and
    leading/trailing separators are stripped.

    Args:
        text: Input text.
        sep: Separator character to use between words.

    Returns:
        The slugified string.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``sep`` is not exactly one character.
    """
    if len(sep) != 1:
        raise ValueError("sep must be a single character")

    pieces: list[str] = []
    previous_was_separator = False
    for char in text.lower():
        if char.isalnum():
            pieces.append(char)
            previous_was_separator = False
        elif not previous_was_separator:
            pieces.append(sep)
            previous_was_separator = True
    return "".join(pieces).strip(sep)

files.src/textkit/wrap.py:
"""Greedy word wrapping."""

from __future__ import annotations


def wrap_text(text: str, width: int) -> list[str]:
    """Wrap ``text`` into lines of at most ``width`` characters.

    Args:
        text: Input text. Runs of whitespace separate words.
        width: Maximum line length. Must be at least 1.

    Returns:
        The wrapped lines, without trailing whitespace. Empty input yields an
        empty list.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``width`` is less than 1.
    """
    if width < 1:
        raise ValueError("width must be at least 1")

    lines: list[str] = []
    current = ""
    for raw_word in text.split():
        word = raw_word
        # A word that cannot fit on any line is hard-split across lines.
        while len(word) > width:
            if current:
                lines.append(current)
                current = ""
            lines.append(word[:width])
            word = word[width:]
        if not word:
            continue
        if not current:
            current = word
        elif len(current) + 1 + len(word) <= width:
            current = f"{current} {word}"
        else:
            lines.append(current)
            current = word

    if current:
        lines.append(current)
    return lines

"""Length-limited text truncation."""

from __future__ import annotations

DEFAULT_SUFFIX = "..."


def truncate(text: str, limit: int, suffix: str = DEFAULT_SUFFIX) -> str:
    """Shorten ``text`` so it fits within ``limit`` characters.

    The returned string never exceeds ``limit``. When the text must be cut, the
    cut is made at a word boundary if one exists inside the available budget.

    Args:
        text: Input text.
        limit: Maximum length of the returned string, including ``suffix``.
        suffix: Marker appended when the text was shortened.

    Returns:
        The original text when it already fits, otherwise a shortened version
        no longer than ``limit``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``limit`` is negative.
    """
    if limit < 0:
        raise ValueError("limit must not be negative")
    if len(text) <= limit:
        return text
    if limit <= len(suffix):
        return suffix[:limit]

    budget = limit - len(suffix)
    head = text[:budget]
    boundary = head.rfind(" ")
    if boundary > 0:
        head = head[:boundary]
    return head.rstrip() + suffix
